title: AI credit worries send default insurance to record high
source_used: Reuters (text read via The Lufkin Daily News, which carries the Reuters wire)
key_facts: Reuters says the cost of insuring against tech defaults hit record highs on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 as investors hedged against credit stress in the AI trade.
Five-year credit default swap spreads for CoreWeave passed 1,100 basis points; its 2031 bond yield rose to as much as 16% before easing to about 14%.
Reuters says a spread of 1,000 basis points implies a 64% risk of default within five years, up from about 30% a year ago.
CoreWeave is a loss-making 'neocloud' company that owes nearly $50 billion, according to LSEG data; its shares fell 15% Wednesday and 2% more Thursday.
Oracle's CDS neared 300 basis points, up about 31 basis points this week; CDS for Amazon, Alphabet and Meta also hit record highs but rose more slowly.
Anthropic's third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, per an investor at a pre-IPO meeting; it targets a $2 trillion valuation.
Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid said a debt-funded capex cycle means credit price action must be respected.
quote_evidence: The cost of insuring against tech defaults struck record highs on Thursday, as investors rushed to hedge against the risk of credit stress building in the AI trade, with heavily indebted data centre operators like CoreWeave hit hardest.
CoreWeave, a loss-making "neocloud" company that owes nearly $50 billion, according to LSEG data, is in the eye of the storm.
A surge in quarterly revenue from AI developer Anthropic did little to calm the market's nerves.
why_it_matters_hint: Credit markets, not only share prices, are now signalling stress over debt-funded AI spending.
